en: The leader of the city of Ayodhyā, the lord of the city of Mithilā, the ornament of the Raghavas, and the adornment of the Videhas. || 1 ||
The lamp of the Raghu dynasty and the lamp of the Nimi dynasty;
born of the solar lineage and born of the lunar lineage.
The first son of Daśaratha and the daughter of King Janaka,
who followed the conduct approved by Vasiṣṭha and adhered to the opinion of Śatānanda.
Born from the womb of Kausalyā, he himself arose from the womb of Vedī;
he whose eyes were as broad as lotuses, and she whose eyes were like shimmering blue water-lilies.
Her lotus-face was as lovely as the moon, her countenance resembling the lunar disc;
her gait was like that of an elephant in rut, and her movement like that of a female swan in heat.
Her waist was moist with sandalwood paste, her breast-region wet with saffron;
her lotus-like hands were adorned with bows, and her palms were decorated with lotuses.
To Rāma, the protector of those who have come for refuge, who is pleased by prostration,
who resembles a dark cloud, and whose splendor is like refined gold.
Seated upon divine thrones, adorned with celestial garlands, garments, and ornaments,
they both longed at every moment to gaze upon one another with their side-long glances.
To you two, husband and wife of the house that is the three worlds, who possess forms so alike one another— I bow and today attain the fulfillment of my purpose by honoring you.
For him who praises with devotion Rāma and Sītā, who are worthy of praise by means of this [work], may those two bestow upon him auspicious prosperities that grant all goals. 10.
Thus, this meritorious hymn, which grants immediate liberation, was composed by Hanumān specifically for Śrī Rāmacandra and Jānakī.
Whoever recites it upon rising in the morning shall attain all desires. (11)
Thus ends the hymn to Sītā and Rāma composed by Hanumān.
